The same result follows from a derivation in vector notation,
which treats $(\intcoef, \coef{x})$ as a single vector
instead of differentiating with respect to each component separately.

::: proof

Collect the coefficients and each observation's covariates into vectors:

$$
\vcoef \eqdef \begin{pmatrix} \intcoef \\ \coef{x} \end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\vxi \eqdef \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ x_i \end{pmatrix},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\intcoef + \coef{x} x_i = \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{RSS}(\vcoef) = \sumin \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}^2.
$$

**Gradient.**
By the chain rule applied to each term of the sum:

$$
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
= \sumin 2 \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
  \deriv{\vcoef} \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}.
$$

For the inner derivative, we need the gradient of a linear function.
For any constant vector $\v{a} = \tp{(a_0, a_x)}$,
$\dprod{\v{a}}{\vcoef} = a_0 \intcoef + a_x \coef{x}$,
whose partial derivatives with respect to $\intcoef$ and $\coef{x}$
are $a_0$ and $a_x$;
so $\deriv{\vcoef} \dprod{\v{a}}{\vcoef} = \v{a}$.
With $\v{a} = \vxi$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\vcoef} \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&= \deriv{\vcoef} y_i - \deriv{\vcoef} \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}
&& \text{(derivative of a difference)}\\
&= \vzero - \vxi
&& \text{($y_i$ does not depend on $\vcoef$; gradient of a linear function)}\\
&= -\vxi
\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the inner derivative back in:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\vcoef} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
&= -2 \sumin \vxi \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-\vxi$)}\\
&= -2 \paren{\sumin \vxi y_i - \sumin \vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}}
&& \text{(distribute the sum)}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Solve for $\hvcoef$.**
Write $A \eqdef \sumin \soprod{\vxi}$ and $\v{c} \eqdef \sumin \vxi y_i$.
Since $\vxi \paren{\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}} = \paren{\soprod{\vxi}} \vcoef$,
the gradient is $-2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}$.
Setting it equal to $\vzero$ gives the
**normal equations** $A \vcoef = \v{c}$.
Writing out the components of each term:

$$
A = \sumin \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x_i \\ x_i & x_i^2 \end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix} n & n\bar{x} \\ n\bar{x} & \sumin x_i^2 \end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\v{c} = \sumin \begin{pmatrix} y_i \\ x_i y_i \end{pmatrix}
= \begin{pmatrix} n\bar{y} \\ \sumin x_i y_i \end{pmatrix}.
$$

The determinant of $A$ is
$n \sumin x_i^2 - n^2 \bar{x}^2 = n S_{xx} > 0$,
so $A$ is invertible and the normal equations have the unique solution

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hvcoef = A^{-1} \v{c}
&= \frac{1}{n S_{xx}}
  \begin{pmatrix} \sumin x_i^2 & -n\bar{x} \\ -n\bar{x} & n \end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix} n\bar{y} \\ \sumin x_i y_i \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{(inverse of a $2 \times 2$ matrix)}\\
&= \frac{1}{S_{xx}}
  \begin{pmatrix}
  \bar{y} \sumin x_i^2 - \bar{x} \sumin x_i y_i \\
  \sumin x_i y_i - n \bar{x} \bar{y}
  \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply, cancel $n$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{S_{xx}}
  \begin{pmatrix}
  \bar{y} \paren{S_{xx} + n\bar{x}^2} - \bar{x} \paren{S_{xy} + n\bar{x}\bar{y}} \\
  S_{xy}
  \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{($\sumin x_i^2 = S_{xx} + n\bar{x}^2$, $\sumin x_i y_i = S_{xy} + n\bar{x}\bar{y}$)}\\
&= \begin{pmatrix}
  \bar{y} - \bar{x} \, S_{xy} / S_{xx} \\
  S_{xy} / S_{xx}
  \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{(first component: cancel $\pm n\bar{x}^2\bar{y}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

which matches $\hintcoef = \bar{y} - \hcoef{x} \bar{x}$
and $\hcoef{x} = S_{xy} / S_{xx}$.

**Second derivative.**
Differentiating the gradient $-2 \paren{\v{c} - A \vcoef}$
with respect to $\tp{\vcoef}$ gives the
[Hessian](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-hessian) of $\text{RSS}$:

$$
\deriv{\vcoef} \deriv{\tp{\vcoef}} \text{RSS}(\vcoef)
= 2 A
= 2 \sumin \soprod{\vxi}.
$$

It is positive definite.
For any vector $\v{v} = \tp{(v_0, v_x)} \neq \vzero$:

$$
\tp{\v{v}} \paren{2 A} \v{v}
= 2 \sumin \paren{\dprod{\v{v}}{\vxi}}^2
= 2 \sumin \paren{v_0 + v_x x_i}^2
\ge 0,
$$

with equality only if $v_0 + v_x x_i = 0$ for every $i$.
If $v_x \neq 0$, that would force every $x_i = -v_0 / v_x$,
contradicting $S_{xx} > 0$;
if $v_x = 0$, it would force $v_0 = 0$,
contradicting $\v{v} \neq \vzero$.
So the inequality is strict,
the Hessian is positive definite at every $\vcoef$,
$\text{RSS}$ is strictly convex,
and $\hvcoef$ is its unique global minimum.

:::
